comments.text_zh: 最近在这里发过的一个很棒的演讲，Michael Levin 教授的《身体在想什么：神经系统之外的生物电计算》[1]。他讲到生物体内所有细胞之间的长期低能量电网络如何塑造生物体的生长。我认为他所讲的内容将是医学的未来，因为它能让你对动物的生长方式实现惊人的高水平控制。1. [VIDEO]
comments.text: Recent but great talk posted here, What Bodies Think About: Bioelectric Computation Outside the Nervous System [1] by Prof. Michael Levin. He talks about how long term low energy electrical networks between all cells in living organisms shape how the organism grows. I think what he talks about will be the future of medicine as it allows for an amazing degree of high level control over how animals grow. 1. [VIDEO]

comments.author: suby

comments.why_zh: 生物电模式独立于基因组存储信息
comments.quote_zh: 我看过的最精彩的演讲之一，就是 2018 年关于这个主题的那场演讲。
comments.text_zh: 我非常期待再过 10 年我们会走到哪一步。医疗和工业应用方面的可能性，怎么夸大似乎都不为过。相关的是，我看过的最精彩的演讲之一，就是 2018 年关于这个主题的那场演讲。它讲到生物似乎拥有生物电模式，这些模式把信息与基因组、解剖状态分开存储。这些生物电模式在发育过程中扮演巨大角色，因为它们似乎在高层次上控制生物体如何构建。作为一个外行和程序员，对我来说这听起来像是：基因组是一个函数的实际实现，而生物电模式是你想要执行的函数序列。他们能够操纵这些生物电模式，做出把一条虫子的尾巴换成另一个头之类的事。想想这里可能实现什么，简直疯狂。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I'm very excited to see where we'll be in another 10 years. The possibilities in terms of medical and industrial applications seems hard to overstate. Related, but one of the best talks I've ever seen was this 2018 talk on the subject. It gets into how organisms seem to have bioelectrical patterns that store information separately from genomic, anatomical states. These bioelectrical patterns play a huge role in developmental processes, as they appear to control how the organism is structured at a high level. As a layman and a programmer, to me it sounds like the genome is the actual implementation of a function and the bioelectrical pattern is the sequence of functions you want to execute. They're able to manipulate these bioelectrical patterns to do things like replace a worms tail with another head. It's absolutely crazy to think about what could be possible here. [VIDEO]

comments.text: Yes, exactly. Is the human body centralized or decentralized? The ego could be said to be the central "pivot" of the system, but then you have the phenomenon of "multiple personalities", and so on. Once you start to think of biology as the study of billion-year-old self-optimizing nanotechnology it makes sense to look to life for models for designing the structure of our own artificial systems. There's the question of what do we want to be like? A starfish? A meta-human? A decentralized system that depends on each or most of its elements to function is a single "point" of failure for the whole. (E.g., a relatively small wound can cause death by exsanguination.) On the other hand, consider the radical indignities that the lowly planarian will endure only to placidly regrow a tail or a head or whatever. (See "What Bodies Think About: Bioelectric Computation Outside the Nervous System" [VIDEO] [LINK] Which, incidentally, adds a whole layer of complexity and nuance to the concept of intelligent design , since the whole of Nature has now been scientifically shown to think ...) comments.author: yehbut99
comments.story_title: Why general artificial intelligence will not be realized
comments.text_zh: 计算机不能自我修复。我们的身体不用有意识地驱动，自己就能做到。人类演化出的是计算机电子状态的复杂度，而不是计算机自身固有的属性。我使用计算机，并不会迫使晶体管演化成更好的晶体管。它没有自我再生能力。你在原则上没看到这个问题，但这里有一篇专家的文章把这些指了出来。也许该更好地听一听？相对于人类的机械功能，计算机有着可观察的、字面意义上的局限。你不能把字面意义上的现实刮掉，去得到某种还原论式的意识概念。对于能创造出我们意识的机器，我们唯一已知的良好模型就是我们自己。宇宙随机翻搅了数十亿年，才偶然产生了我们。我们完全不知道如何复制那种规模。一台计算机字面意义上缺少大量字面意义上的信息，而这些信息嵌入在一个人的硬件和软件之中。看看这个，然后告诉我，上一次你改变计算机的电场属性时，它重新配置自己字面意义上的形状是什么时候：[VIDEO]“生命”中有某种东西，是我们永远无法塞进硅里的。
comments.text: Computers can’t heal themselves. Our bodies do that on their own without conscious prompting. Humans evolve the complexity of a computers electron states, not the computers own inherent properties. My use doesn’t force transistors to evolve into better transistors. It has no self regeneration. You don’t see the issue in principle but here you have an article by an expert pointing them out. Perhaps be a better listener? A computer has observable, literal limitations relative to a humans mechanical functionality. You can’t scrape away literal reality to arrive at some reductionist idea of what a consciousness is. Our only known good model for a machine that can create our consciousness is us. It took billions of years of the universe churning at random to accidentally generate us. We have no clue how to replicate that scale. A computer literally lacks a whole lot of literal information that’s embedded in the hardware and software of a person. Watch this and tell me the last time your computer reconfigured it’s literal shape when you altered its electric field properties: [VIDEO] There’s something to “life” we’ll never be able to jam into silicon.

comments.why_zh: 按 Levin 实验室的工作，细胞都会思考
comments.quote_zh: 看看 Michael Levin 实验室工作近来的科学进展
comments.text_zh:
> 如上所述，单个植物并不是朋友，而是其物种的精神。
对。
> 我没办法真正理解这一切。
你当然可以！你也是一个活生生的生命，对吧？:) 你拥有全部硬件，只是需要学会协议。学起来没那么难，最难的部分可以说是“放下拘束”。看看 Michael Levin 实验室工作近来的科学进展，例如 “What Bodies Think About: Bioelectric Computation Outside the Nervous System” - NeurIPS 2018 [VIDEO] [LINK] [LINK] 简而言之，无论“思考”是什么，支撑它的生物分子机制在所有细胞中都是共通的（不只是神经元）。换句话说，所有细胞生命都会“思考”。把这个洞见与控制论中的“调节模型定律”结合起来，即：“任何系统的良好调节器都必须（包含）该系统的一个模型。”在我看来，我们就有坚实的基础来谈论“自然精灵”了，对吧？
comments.text: > As described, the individual plant is not the friend, but rather the spirit of its species. Aye. > I have no way to properly apprehend any of this. Sure you do! You're a living being too, eh? :) You've got all the hardware, you just need to learn the protocols. It's not that hard to learn, the hardest part is "letting your hair down" so to speak. Check out the recent scientific advances from Michael Levin's lab's work, e.g. "What Bodies Think About: Bioelectric Computation Outside the Nervous System" - NeurIPS 2018 [VIDEO] [LINK] [LINK] In a nutshell, whatever "thought" is, the biomolecular machinery that supports it is common to all cells (not just neurons.) In other words, all cellular life "thinks". Combine that insight with the "Law Of Regulatory Models" from Cybernetics, to wit: "every good regulator of a system must be (contain) a model of that system." and it seems to me that we have a solid basis to talk about "nature spirits", eh?
